entries.name: # Voice of the Daelkyr
entries: You can speak with any Aberration as if you shared a language.

entries.name: # Command Aberration
entries: As a Magic action, you can cast {@spell Dominate Monster|XPHB} on an Aberration (save DC 18). Once this property is used, you cannot do so again until the next dawn.

entries.name: # Petrifying Touch
entries: The power of the stone shaper flows from you—despite what you may will. Any creature that you touch with your stone fingertips is affected as if you had cast {@spell Flesh to Stone|XPHB} (spell save DC 18). You do not need to concentrate on the effect, and you cannot choose to end it.

entries.name: # Stone Speaking
entries: As a Magic action, you imbue stones in an immobile 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} with limited sentience, giving them the ability to communicate with you. You can question stones about events in the effects area within the past day, gaining information about creatures that have passed, items that might have been removed from the area, and other circumstances. If an earth elemental or {@condition Petrified|XPHB} creature is in the area, you can communicate with it as if you shared a common language, but you gain no magical ability to influence it.

entries.name: # Greater Symbiotic Nature
entries: The arm can't be removed from you while you're attuned to it, and you can't voluntarily end your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to it. Your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to the arm can only be ended by a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell.

item.name: Living Stoneskin
entries: This Plate Armor appears to be made of stone slabs carved with alien symbols. It is strangely warm to the touch. To attune to this item, you must wear it for the entire {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} period, during which the stone plates fuse with your skin.

While wearing this armor, you have a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}, and you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to nonmagical Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage. Additionally, the armor hardens under extreme impact; if you take 20 or more nonmagical Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage from one damage roll (after accounting for your {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB}), you are {@condition Petrified|XPHB} until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: # Symbiotic Nature
entries: The armor can't be removed from you while you're attuned to it, and you can't voluntarily end your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to it. If you're targeted by a spell that ends a curse, your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to the armor ends, and it detaches from you.

The armor requires fresh blood be fed to it. Immediately after you finish any {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you must either feed half of your remaining Hit Dice to the armor (round up) or take 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}.

item.name: Ink's Aide
entries: This colorful, jellyfish-like blob has been carefully cultivated by Quickstone's schoolmaster, Tragomir "Ink" Narathun, to impart a full curriculum to its host—though he has yet to convince anyone to partake. To attune to this item, you must hold it to one ear for the full {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} period, during which time its stringy tentacles reach inside your ear canal and secure the aide in place. The symbiont does not impair your hearing while it is attached.

entries.name: Spells
entries: The symbiont has 4 charges. You can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 15) from it: {@spell Enhance Ability|XPHB} (2 charges) or {@spell Comprehend Languages|XPHB} (1 charge).
The symbiont regains {@dice 1d4} expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: The aide can't be removed from you while you're attuned to it, and you can't voluntarily end your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to it. If you're targeted by a spell that ends a curse, your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to the aide ends, and it detaches from your ear.

item.name: Kharash's Promise
entries: Tol Kharash, the Horned King, overlord of tyranny, demands that his minions revel in domination, fear, and the suffering of the downtrodden. During his campaigns in the Age of Demons, Tol Kharash shaped an artifact that would announce his coming across the Barrens; a harbinger of cruelty.

Kharash's Promise is a 3-foot long warhorn forged of demonglass and black iron. A trickle of boiling blood constantly drips from its widest end. While holding this Horn, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your Bard spells.

entries.name: Random Properties.
entries: This Artifact has the following random properties, which you can determine by rolling on the tables in the "Artifacts" section of the Dungeon Master's Guide:

items: 2 {@table Artifact Properties; Minor Beneficial Properties|XDMG|minor beneficial} properties
1 {@table Artifact Properties; Major Beneficial Properties|XDMG|major beneficial} property
2 {@table Artifact Properties; Minor Detrimental Properties|XDMG|minor detrimental} properties

entries.name: Surety of Dominance
entries: While attuned to the warhorn, no creature can assert its influence over you. You cannot be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB}. If a creature targets you with a magical effect that would cause you to be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, that creature takes {@damage 4d10} Psychic damage.

entries.name: Thaumaturgic Clarion
entries: If you blow Kharash's Promise, the sound it produces can be heard by all creatures within 1 mile.

entries.name: Promised End
entries: As a Magic action when you blow the horn, you can choose one creature that you can see and that can hear the horn to suffer a painful and inevitable end. The target must make a DC 20 Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the target's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced by 1 at the start of each of its turns until it dies, you die, you are no longer on the same plane of existence as the target, or the effect is ended with a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell. Once this property is used, you cannot do so again until 13 days have passed.
As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while affected, the target can choose to confront the source of its inevitable end, teleporting to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.

item.name: Demonglass Weapon

entries: A demonglass shard is inlaid into this weapon, granting it magical properties. Though the fiendish presence embedded within cannot speak directly to its wielder, its presence is keenly felt by those whose blood it spills.

You have a {=bonusWeapon} bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. On a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}, the target is {@condition Frightened|XPHB} of you until the end of its next turn, and you gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws until the end of your next turn.

entries: Tommybows are repeating crossbows that mirror the three types of normal crossbows: hand, heavy, and light. They are composed of vertically-stacked bows upon a crossbow's chassis, an unwieldy arrangement that reduces their effective range in comparison to their crossbow counterparts.

base.name: Hooked Shortspear
entries: On a hit with this weapon, the wielder can forgo dealing damage and attempt to trip the target, in which case the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or fall {@condition prone}. The DC is 8 + the wielder's Strength modifier + the wielder's proficiency bonus.

specificVariant.name: Demonglass Hooked Shortspear

base.name: Hoopak
entries: A hoopak is a sturdy stick with a sling at one end and a pointed tip at the other.

entries.name: Special
entries: When you make a melee attack with this weapon, you ignore its ammunition property. You can use the hoopak as a martial ranged weapon. If you do, it uses the ammunition property, uses sling bullets, and deals {@damage 1d4} bludgeoning damage on a hit.

base.name: Lance
entries: A Lance requires two hands to wield when you aren't mounted.

specificVariant.name: Demonglass Lance
entries: A Lance requires two hands to wield when you aren't mounted.

entries.name: Special
entries: You have disadvantage on attacks made with a bayonet that isn't attached to a crossbow. It takes an action to attach or remove a bayonet from a weapon.

entries.name: Special
entries: You have disadvantage on attacks made with a bayonet that isn't attached to a crossbow. It takes an action to attach or remove a bayonet from a weapon.

base.name: Light Repeating Crossbow
entries: This crossbow is fitted with a cartridge that can hold up to six crossbow bolts. It automatically reloads after firing until the cartridge runs out of ammunition. Reloading the cartridge takes an action.

specificVariant.name: Demonglass Light Repeating Crossbow
entries: This crossbow is fitted with a cartridge that can hold up to six crossbow bolts. It automatically reloads after firing until the cartridge runs out of ammunition. Reloading the cartridge takes an action.

base.name: Yklwa
entries: A yklwa (pronounced YICK-ul-wah) is a simple melee weapon that is the traditional weapon of Chultan warriors. A yklwa consists of a 3-foot wooden shaft with a steel or stone blade up to 18 inches long. Although it has the thrown weapon property, the yklwa is not well balanced for throwing.

specificVariant.name: Demonglass Yklwa
entries: A yklwa (pronounced YICK-ul-wah) is a simple melee weapon that is the traditional weapon of Chultan warriors. A yklwa consists of a 3-foot wooden shaft with a steel or stone blade up to 18 inches long. Although it has the thrown weapon property, the yklwa is not well balanced for throwing.

item.name: Demonglass Orb
entries: Red and black flames flicker behind the rough cut facets of this heavy demonglass shard. Memories of the Ages of Demons are bound within, and spellcasters who dare channel their magic through it find themselves and their targets visited by visions of that terrible past.

Whenever you cast a Divination spell using this Orb as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}, you can give up some of your life force to reduce the saving throw of one creature affected by your spell. Roll 1 to 4 d6s; the resulting total is how much Necrotic damage you take. This damage can't be reduced in any way. The target has its saving throw reduced by 1 for each {@damage d6} of damage you take. You must decide how many dice to roll before the DM says whether the target succeeds or fails.

item.name: Brand of Tyranny
entries: One end of this heavy, black iron Rod glows as if hot. Rather than burning red and orange, it shines a sickly shade of purple.
While holding this Rod, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your spells.

Whenever you touch a creature with this Rod, that creature must succeed on a DC 15 Charisma saving throw or be branded with the mark of Tol Kharash, the overlord known as the Horned King. Whenever a branded creature makes an attack roll or a saving throw against being {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, the creature must roll a {@dice d4} and subtract the number rolled from the attack roll or saving throw. The brand lasts until the next dawn or it is removed with Remove {@variantrule Curses|XPHB|Curse} or Greater Restoration.

item.name: Thunder Coach
item.reqAttune: by a creature with the mark of passage
entries: The Thunder Coach is the workhorse of Orien's overland shipping, sometimes referred to as "galleons of the road." A product of the Twelve, it incorporated members of Kundarak, Cannith, and Orien in the design. A typical coach is a 10-foot-wide, 40-foot-long, 15-foot-high (including the wheels) vessel of wood and steel. When pulled by a large team (typically eight tribex), a coach can maintain a speed of up to five miles per hour. However, if someone with the Mark of Passage attunes to the coach and sits in the driver's seat, the full magic of the Thunder Coach comes into play. Under such conditions, four strong beasts can pull the coach at a steady pace of ten miles an hour. If it is moving along an Orien trade road, the effect is further amplified, allowing a top speed of 15 miles per hour. This requires the driver to remain seated and to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}, as if casting a spell. However, beyond these limitations, they are capable of conversation and other actions.

The forward fifteen feet of the coach holds a small cabin for up to three crew members. The crew of a coach typically includes one marked driver and two crew members who serve as both guards and cargo haulers. One of these haulers is usually a Vadalis- trained (though unmarked) handler who cares for the beasts. The top of the coach has positions at the front and back where archers or wandslingers can be stationed with {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover}.

A typical Thunder Coach has two cargo chambers; one magical and one mundane. The back gate of a Thunder Coach opens to grant access to an extradimensional space that functions in the same way as a {@item Bag of Holding|XDMG}. When closed, the gate is typically sealed with an Arcane Lock linked to a password known to the driver. The mouth of the extradimensional space is 10-feet-wide by 10-feet-high. The size of the extradimensional space varies based on the model of the coach; the standard is 20-feet-wide, 15-feet-high, and 50-feet-deep. The system maintaining the extradimensional space takes up the final five feet of the coach.

Objects that produce extradimensional spaces (such as Bags of Holding, Portable Holes, or House Cannith's Crates of Containing) cannot cross the threshold of the rear compartment. For this reason, and to allow the transport of living creatures, the Thunder Coach also has a standard cargo compartment accessed from the side of the vehicle; this space is 10-feet-wide, 10-feet- high, and 20-feet-long.

item.name: Three-Faced Coin
entries: This gold piece appears to be a normal coin, with the crown of Galifar on one side and the Octogram of the Sovereign Host on the other. However, when flipped, it will land with one of three different symbols showing, each corresponding to one of the patrons of the Three Faces of Coin: Kol Korran, Onatar, and Kol Turrant (the Keeper). When you flip the coin, you can will the coin to land displaying a face of your choice. Once this property is used, you cannot do so again until the next dawn.

While this item doesn't require a command word or {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, the ability must be consciously triggered; if you've never used a Three-faced coin before, you must spend a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} studying it to learn how to activate it. After being flipped, the coin returns to its usual two faces when a creature next touches it.

item.name: Stonebane Weapon

entries: This weapon was masterfully crafted by artificers of the ancient Dhakaani empire to combat the minions of the daelkyr Orlassk. It is forged from byeshk, and does not corrode or weather with time.

Although stonebane weapons are not inherently magical, this weapon ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to nonmagical Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage when used against creatures made of stone, creatures with stone-like natural armor (such as Gargoyles), and {@condition Petrified|XPHB} creatures.

As with other byeshk weapons, this weapon is especially effective against Aberrations. Whenever you hit an Aberration with this weapon, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} damage of the weapon's type, and it can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} until the start of your next turn.
This weapon was masterfully crafted by artificers of the ancient Dhakaani empire to combat the minions of the daelkyr Orlassk. It is forged from byeshk, and does not corrode or weather with time.

Although stonebane weapons are not inherently magical, this weapon ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to nonmagical Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage when used against creatures made of stone, creatures with stone-like natural armor (such as Gargoyles), and {@condition Petrified|XPHB} creatures.

As with other byeshk weapons, this weapon is especially effective against Aberrations. Whenever you hit an Aberration with this weapon, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} damage of the weapon's type, and it can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} until the start of your next turn.

base.name: Lance
entries: A Lance requires two hands to wield when you aren't mounted.

specificVariant.name: Stonebane Lance
entries: A Lance requires two hands to wield when you aren't mounted.

item.name: Shock and Ore
entries: This pair of rough and ready War Picks are said to have been created by the first miners to quarry quickstone in the Barrens. They have long been passed around as heirlooms and rewards. These magical picks are a single magic item for the purposes of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}.
You gain the following benefits while wielding both picks:

items: The picks have the Light weapon property.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with the picks.
The picks have 3 charges, which they share. They regain {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn.

When you hit a target with a Melee attack using Shock, you can expend 1 charge as a bonus action to deal an additional {@damage 2d8} Lightning damage. A creature affected by this damage can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
When you hit a target with a Melee attack using Ore, you can expend 1 charge to cast {@spell Earth Tremor|XGE} XGE as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, centered on the target.

item.name: Scale of Kethelrax
entries: This Dagger is said to have been created by Kethelrax the Cunning, the kobold warlord of Shaarat Kol. Its short, crimson blade resembles a red dragon's scale, and tiny flames dance along its edge.

While you are holding this Dagger, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells. Additionally, you can cast {@spell Fire Bolt|XPHB} as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, using Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (you choose when you Attune to the dagger) as the spellcasting ability.
Whenever you hit with a weapon attack using this Dagger, you can choose to deal Fire damage instead of Piercing damage.

item.name: Sarkaas' Gladrags
entries: Deven Sarkaas of Littlehand Haberdashers in Quickstone knows all too well how important it is to look one's best... and how 'best' can be very different depending on who (or what) you're meeting with. Deven stitched this fine cloak and sent it to Graywall to be enchanted, only to lose track of the garment on the return journey.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while wearing the cloak, you can speak its command word to transform your outfit into finely crafted garments appropriate to the culture of one creature of your choice that you can see. Regardless of its appearance, the outfit can't be anything but clothing. Although it can duplicate the look of other magical clothing, the outfit doesn't gain its magical properties.

item.name: Sandstorm Staff
entries: Many of the discarded weapons of the Last War have found their way into the hands of the people of the Barrens. This sliver of a broken Siege Staff can deliver a powerful punch when it needs to, but ejects an exhaust of swirling dust when exerted.
This staff can be wielded as a magic Quarterstaff. The staff has 10 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn.

When you cast a spell using this Staff as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}, you can expend 1 charge to gain a +1 bonus to all spell attack rolls you make for that spell. If you do so, the staff conjures a 5-foot diameter vortex of dust in your space. At the start of each of your turns, roll a {@dice d20} for each dust vortex the staff has created. On a roll of 11 or higher, the dust vortex moves 5 feet in a random direction. On a roll of 10 or less, the dust vortex disappears.

Any creature that starts its turn within 5 feet of any of the dust vortexes must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, an affected creature takes {@damage 1d4} Bludgeoning damage and is {@condition Blinded|XPHB} until the end of its turn.

item.name: Quickstone Boomstick
entries: Whenever you cast a spell of 1st-level or higher using this Rod as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}, you can choose to release its power in a thunderous burst. All creatures within 5 feet of you (including you) must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, affected creatures take {@damage 1d4} Thunder damage for each level of the spell you cast, and are {@condition Deafened|XPHB} until the end of their next turn.

item.name: Misthaven Miscellany
entries: This small embroidered pouch is said to contain the cast-off goods discarded by the Merchant of Misthaven, an archfey of Thelanis. When you reach into the pouch, you can pull out a random trinket (see page 46 of the 2024 version of the fifth edition Player's Handbook or any other random trinket table of your choice). A trinket pulled from this pouch disappears when you pull another trinket from the pouch.

item.name: Lightning Runner
entries: This 10-foot-wide, 10-foot-long, 6-inch-thick platform of wood and steel levitates 5 feet off the ground and remains horizontal so long as it is within 20 feet of an operational track of lightning rail conductor stones. The platform can carry up to 2000 pounds. If it becomes overloaded, it drops to the ground, unable to levitate.

The platform is equipped with a 'pump' in its center that can be used to move it along the track of conductor stones. As a Magic action, a creature touching the pump can expend a spell slot of 1st-level or higher to cause the platform to continuously move either forwards or backwards along the conductor stone track at a speed of 30 feet. A creature with the Mark of Passage does not need to expend a spell slot to cause the platform to move.

Once moving, the platform will move in the chosen direction for one hour, or until a creature touching the pump uses a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cause the platform to stop. If stopped in this way, a creature must expend another spell slot as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to start the platform moving again.

If the platform encounters an obstacle while moving, it will continue to push against the obstacle unless stopped with a {@action Magic|XPHB} action. Obstacles that weigh less than the total weight of the platform and its cargo will be pushed in front of the platform.

item.name: Jury's Squeaky Wheel
entries: This magic Shield resembles a wooden wagon wheel. Writing inscribed on its inner rim indicates the shield was crafted by Jury d'Cannith, Quickstone's premier artificer, to prove a point to her wife.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while holding this shield, you can grant {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your level to the humanoid creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that has the fewest {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. If creatures you can see within range are tied for the fewest {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can choose which of those creatures gains the {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

item.name: Flashdraw Wand
entries: This delicate Wand hums with bound potential, and seems drawn to your fingers. While attuned to it, you cannot be {@status Surprised|XPHB}. Additionally, whenever you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} you can choose to immediately draw this wand (no action required). If you do so, you can roll {@dice 1d4} and add the total to your {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} score, and all creatures within 5 feet of you take 1 Lightning damage.

item.name: Duelist's Scorecard
entries: This scrap of paper bears a table with space for five names. If you write a creature's name in one of the blank spaces on the table, it will shuffle the text to show their ranking as a duelist relative to all the other individuals named on the table. This appears to be calculated based on the number of duels the named individuals have won over the past year. The source of these scorecards and the rankings remains a mystery, but it appears to be linked to the Infinite Archive of Daanvi. Once all the spaces on the scorecard are filled, you cannot reveal the ranking of another name for 1 week, when all the names are magically erased.

item.name: Dry Spell
entries: This desiccated {@item Spell Scroll|XPHB} seems to draw the moisture from your fingertips. Its cipher is ineffable, and while its meaning becomes clear as you read the runes, clarity slips away should you try to transcribe it.

As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can use the scroll to cast {@spell Control Water|XPHB} without providing any Material components. The spell save DC is 15. In addition to the usual effects of the {@spell Control Water|XPHB} spell, any water manipulated by the spell is destroyed when the spell ends. Once the spell is cast, the words on the scroll fade, and it crumbles to dust. If the casting is interrupted, the scroll is not lost.

item.name: Daff's Wonderful Draught
entries: Daff d'Jorasco's eclectic style of medicine produces similarly eclectic brews. This potion is a magic item. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can drink it or administer it to another creature within 5 of yourself. The creature that drinks this potion must roll on the following table to determine the effect:

entries.caption: Potion Effects
rows: You gain the effects of the {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB} spell for 1 minute or until you lose your {@variantrule Concentration|XPHB}. The save DC is 13.
You gain the effects of the {@spell Haste|XPHB} spell for 1 minute or until you lose your {@variantrule Concentration|XPHB}.
You must succeed on a {@dc 13} Wisdom saving throw or suffer the effects of the {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|XPHB} spell for 1 minute.

item.name: Beggar's Wisdom
entries: The wit and wisdom of Beggar Dane is considered to be one of the national treasures of Breland. This small leatherbound book is a comprehensive, enchanted edition of his proverbs and advice. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action while holding this book, you can declare your desire for assistance with a particular task, causing the book to open to a page containing a quip or mote of wisdom that is strangely relevant to the situation at hand. You add {@dice 1d4} to the next ability check you make within the next minute. Once this property is used, you cannot benefit from any copy of {@i Beggar's Wisdom} until the next dawn.

item.name: Sun Eater's Soul
entries: This black metal ring is unnervingly matte, reflecting nothing even in the brightest of light. While wearing this ring, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of you is hit with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the damage that creature takes from the attack. The ring can be used to halve damage three times and regains all uses daily at dusk.

entries.name: Sun Eater's Grace
entries: When you cast a spell that restores hit points to a creature, you can also restore that same number of hit points to a creature within 30 feet of you who is attuned to the Sun Eater's mind. The ring can be used to restore hit points three times and regains all uses daily at dusk.

item.name: Sun Eater's Mind
entries: The shifting shadows within this black glass ring constantly move. While wearing this ring, when a creature you can see within 60 feet of you makes a spell attack against you or casts a spell that requires you to make a saving throw, you can use your reaction to pierce the creature's mind. The next attack you make against that creature before the end of your next turn is automatically a critical hit. The ring can be used to pierce a creature's mind three times and regains all uses daily at dusk.

entries.name: Sun Eater's Gift
entries: While within 30 feet of a willing creature who is attuned to the Sun Eater's soul, you can use a bonus action to swap places with them. The ring can be used to swap places three times and regains all uses daily at dusk.

item.name: Visionary's Cloak
entries: This gray, hooded traveler's cloak sports a white silk hem and a platinum clasp that, when closed, resembles the shape of an eye.
While wearing this cloak, you have advantage on initiative checks and can't be surprised.

Additionally, when you wear the cloak with the hood up, you gain {@sense truesight} out to a range of 60 feet and your eyes cast a soft blue-white glow. Pulling the hood up or down requires an action.

entries.name: Cursed Sentience
entries: The cloak is a sentient and cursed magic item, as described {@book above|FleeMortals|3|Magic Items|4}.

item.name: Ring of Scarlet Shadows
entries: This iridium ring is inlaid with an obsidian band. The stone inlay occasionally appears to writhe or shift, as if shadows play along its surface.

While wearing this ring, you gain {@sense darkvision} out to a range of 60 feet, or if you already have {@sense darkvision}, its range increases by 60 feet. Additionally, you have advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks made to hide.

entries.name: Shadow Blade
entries: You can use a bonus action to extend a blade of shadows from the hand that wears the ring. You can wield the blade as a shortsword that deals necrotic damage instead of piercing damage. While the blade is extended, you can't drop it or hold anything else in that hand. You can dismiss the blade as a bonus action.

entries.name: Cursed Sentience
entries: The ring is a sentient and cursed magic item, as described {@book above|FleeMortals|3|Magic Items|4}.

item.name: Pathfinder's Boots
entries: Silver eyelets decorate these soft leather boots. While wearing these boots, you gain a +2 bonus to your AC and your walking speed increases by 10 feet.

The boots have 7 charges. While wearing them, you can expend 1 charge to cast one of the following spells from them: {@spell feather fall}, {@spell jump}, or {@spell shield}. The boots regain {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Cursed Sentience
entries: The boots are a sentient and cursed magic item, as described {@book above|FleeMortals|3|Magic Items|4}.

item.name: Crown of Majesty
entries: This mithral circlet is inscribed with an intricate filigree formed of Elvish runes. The front of the circlet holds a flawless diamond that changes hue in sunlight.
While wearing this crown, you have resistance to psychic damage, and you can't be {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened}.

The crown has 3 charges. While wearing it, you can use an action and expend 1 charge to cast one of the following spells from it (save DC 18): {@spell command} or {@spell charm person}. The crown regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Cursed Sentience
entries: The crown is a sentient and cursed magic item, as described {@book above|FleeMortals|3|Magic Items|4}.

item.name: Bracers of the Spellbreaker
entries: These mithral bracers are engraved with runes and inlaid with three multicolored bands of tiny gemstones.
While wearing these bracers, you have advantage on saving throws against spells and magical effects. In addition, damage from your spell attacks ignore your target's damage resistances.

entries.name: Cursed Sentience
entries: The bracers are a sentient and cursed magic item, as described {@book above|FleeMortals|3|Magic Items|4}.

item.name: Mindrazor
entries: This rapier was forged using shattered fragments of a powerful psionic crystal and ore from a falling star. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

This rapier has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a creature with an attack roll using this weapon, you can expend 1 charge to attempt to inflict a psionic wound. The target must succeed on a DC 17 Intelligence saving throw or become vulnerable to psychic damage for 1 minute (save ends at end of turn).

item.name: Amethyst Die
entries: This gaming die is carved from a fragment of powerful psionic crystal and resonates with a remnant of its power. This die has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. When you make an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw, you can expend 1 charge to roll a {@dice d6} and add the number rolled to the {@dice d20} roll. Immediately after the ability check, attack roll, or saving throw is resolved, you take psychic damage equal to twice the number you rolled on the {@dice d6}.

item.name: Waning Moon
entries: This slender elven bow is lacquered blue and purple.
Its inside curve twinkles with tiny diamonds set like a field of stars.
This magical longbow grants a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. If you hit a creature who can't see you with this bow, the attack deals an extra {@damage 2d6} force damage.
Additionally, when you hit a target with an attack made with the bow, you can choose to become {@condition invisible} for 1 minute and take the {@action Hide} action as part of the attack.
The invisibility ends early if you attack, cast a spell, or manifest a power. Once this invisibility has been used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

item.name: Eye of Sunrise
entries: A crimson gemstone glitters on the back of this black iron gauntlet. While wearing the gauntlet, you can use a bonus action to cause the stone to shed bright red light in a 10-foot radius and {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} for an additional 10 feet. You can use another bonus action to extinguish the light.

Additionally, you can use an action to raise the gauntlet and emit a fiery explosion in a 30-foot cone. The explosion can be heard 300 feet away. Each creature in the area must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 5d6} fire damage plus {@damage 5d6} force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Each structure and mundane object in the area that isn't being worn or carried takes {@damage 10d6} fire damage plus {@damage 10d6} force damage. Once this action is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: (Requires Attunement)
entries: This magic maul is made of a durable, light metal and has a long haft, giving it a reach of 10 feet. When you hit a creature with this maul, they are hexed until the end of their next turn. Whenever a creature hexed in this way makes an attack roll or saving throw, they must roll a {@dice d4} and subtract the number rolled from the attack roll or saving throw.
While you hold the maul, you can use an action to change the appearance of its head, choosing its shape and color.

item.name: Iron Ring
entries: While wearing this ring, you can use an action to speak a passphrase known only to the High Command of the Black Iron Pact—"Blood of Rioja"—and choose a target destination. If you are not in the demiplane known as the Cyst, you must choose a destination within the Cyst. If you are already in the Cyst, you must choose a destination you have visited before. Once you choose a destination in this way, the ring teleports you there. The ring can be used to teleport twice and regains both uses daily at dusk.

entries.name: Curse
entries: Once you attune to this ring, you can't take it off or end your attunement to it unless you are targeted by a {@psionic cure ailment|TalPsi} power of 4th order or higher or the {@spell greater restoration} spell.

item.name: Poison Popper
entries: You can throw this inedible fruit at a point you can see within 60 feet of you, causing it to explode and release a cloud of noxious gas in a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on that point. The cloud spreads around corners and lingers for 1 minute. A moderate wind (at least 10 miles per hour) disperses the cloud after 4 rounds. A strong wind (at least 20 miles per hour) disperses it after 1 round.

The cloud's area is {@quickref Vision and Light||2||lightly obscured}, and when a creature enters it for the first time on a turn or starts their turn there, they must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 14 ({@damage 4d6}) poison damage and is {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute (save ends at end of turn). While {@condition poisoned} in this way, a creature's speed is halved. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and suffers no other effect.

item.name: Boog's Ball
entries: This magic stone sphere is incredibly dense, has a 3-inch radius, and grows when thrown. As an action, you can throw the ball at a point you can see within 60 feet of you. If you throw the ball 30 feet or less away from you, the ball grows to a 5-foot radius. If you throw the ball farther than 30 feet, it grows to a 10-foot radius. Each creature in the ball's area when it reaches that point must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 14 ({@damage 4d6}) bludgeoning damage. The ball then shrinks back to its 3-inch radius and teleports either into your open hand or into a pack or pouch you wear (your choice).

item.name: Tome of the Ethereal
entries: Lighter than it rightly should be, this book is always cold to the touch and blurs when seen in periphery. While holding the tome, you can see into the Ethereal Plane out to a range of 120 feet.

In addition, the tome has 3 charges, and it regains all expended charges daily at dusk. When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you targets you with a power, a spell, or an attack while you aren't on the Ethereal Plane, you can use your reaction to expend 1 charge and choose one of the following effects:

items: You enter the Ethereal Plane, then return to the plane and the space you left at the start of your next turn.

entries: If that space is occupied, you return to the nearest unoccupied space of your choice.

items: You teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

item.name: Pendant of Grave Regeneration
entries: While you wear this pendant, your skin becomes pale and cold to the touch, and you regain 5 hit points at the start of your turn if you have at least 1 hit point.

entries.name: Curse
entries: Attuning to this pendant extends its curse to you. Until the curse is broken with a remove curse spell or similar magic, you can't take it off, and your creature type is Undead instead of your normal type.

item.name: Treant Arrow
entries: This arrow is carved from the boughs of a living {@creature treant|FleeMortals}.

When a creature takes damage from the arrow, they are {@condition restrained} by vines that sprout from the shaft. A creature can make a {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check as an action, freeing themself or another creature {@condition restrained} by the arrow within their reach on a success.
Once a treant arrow restrains a creature or if the treant used to make the arrow dies, it becomes a mundane arrow.

item.name: Mantle of the Lightbender
entries: This elegant cloak is lined with the iridescent mane of a {@creature lightbender|FleeMortals}. When you're hit with an attack while wearing this cloak, you can use your reaction to reveal that the attacker is attacking a past visual imprint of you. You appear in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of your imprint, the attack misses, then the imprint disappears. You can't use this reaction if the attacker relies on senses other than sight, such as {@sense blindsight}, or if they can perceive illusions as false, as with {@sense truesight}. Once you use the cloak to reveal a past visual imprint of yourself, you can't do so again until the next dawn.

item.name: Charlatan's Gloves
entries: While wearing these gloves, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to produce an illusory image that fits in the palm of your hand. The image lasts for 1 minute or until your {@status Concentration|XPHB} ends (as if you were {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating} on a spell). The image can't create sound, light, smell, or any other sensory effect. Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, because things can pass through it.

If a creature takes a {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the image, the creature can determine that it is an illusion with a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check contested by your Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) check. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the illusion becomes faint to the creature.

item.name: Battle Rod
entries: The Battle Rod was developed as an alternative to the longer {@item War Staff|ExploringEberron24}, and has gained popularity with wandslingers across Khorvaire. When held in two hands, you can use the rod to cast cantrips at up to twice the standard range. However, when you cast a cantrip beyond the standard range, your attack rolls have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}, and targets have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws made against your cantrip. For example, a {@spell Fire Bolt|XPHB} cast using this rod has a range of 240 feet, but attack rolls against targets more than 120 feet away are made at {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

item.name: Wind Stones
entries: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Scribing|EFA}}

Sending Stones come in pairs, with each stone carved to match the other so the pairing is easily recognized. While you touch one stone, you can cast {@spell Sending|XPHB} from it. The target is the bearer of the other stone. If no creature bears the other stone, you know that fact as soon as you use the stone, and you don't cast the spell.
Once Sending is cast using either stone, the stones can't be used again until the next dawn. If one of the stones in a pair is destroyed, the other one becomes nonmagical.

item.name: Warding Dragonmark Reservoir
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA}
entries: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

item.name: Warding Dragonmark Channel
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA}
entries: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.

While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

item.name: Warding Channeling Wand
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA}
entries: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

items.name: Casting Time
entries: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 {@action Magic|XPHB} action to instead be cast as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Duration
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.

items.name: Range
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.

items.name: Regaining Charges
entries: The wand regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

item.name: Warding Brooch
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA}
entries: While wearing this brooch, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Force damage, and you have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to damage from the {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB} spell.

item.name: War Staff
entries: Aundair developed this staff to help wandslingers match the range of Thrane archers, but it quickly spread across Khorvaire. While holding this staff in both hands, you can use it as an {@item Arcane Focus|XPHB}. Any cantrip cast using the staff can be cast at up to four times the standard range. However, when you cast a cantrip at more than twice the standard range, your attack rolls have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}, and targets have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws made against your cantrip. For example, a {@spell Fire Bolt|XPHB} cast using this staff has a range of 480 feet, but attack rolls against targets more than 240 feet away are made at {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

item.name: Wandering Eye
entries: This disturbing daelkyr-made symbiont is a leathery tentacle with one end terminating in a single bulbous eye, and the other sporting a barb designed to burrow into flesh. When you attune to the eye, it burrows into one of your shoulders, then rises up from it, studying the world and projecting insights into your mind. The eye may occasionally take an interest in some random element of your current environment; in this case, the DM may draw your attention to this object or person.
While the eye is uncovered, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Always Vigilant
entries: The eye remains watchful while you sleep. When you take a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, the eye remains active, allowing you to use your Passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) score to notice threats even while asleep. If the eye spots danger, it sends you a mental alarm in the form of a nightmare that immediately wakes you up.

entries.name: Periscopic Vision
entries: The eye can stretch up to 18 inches and can be used to peer around corners or over cover. When extended and used in this way, the eye has an AC of 20 and 6 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. If it is forced to make an ability check or a saving throw, it uses your statistics. If it is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you cannot benefit from any of the eye's properties until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, after which it regains all lost {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Third Eye
entries: When you make a Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check involving sight, you can roll {@dice 1d4} and add the number rolled to the ability check.

entries.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

item.name: Vola'khesh
entries: This small carved stone is typically bound to a leather strap worn around the wrist or neck. Designed by the Dhakaani duur'kala, the Vola'khesh facilitates communication between elite units. They are created in linked sets; up to ten stones can be bound together, and once established, this link cannot be changed. At present, the Vola'khesh are only used by the Kech Dhakaan and are unknown to the people of the Five Nations. If the enchantments were replicated, these tools could be put into use by spies and law enforcement agencies of the Five Nations.

While wearing a Vola'khesh, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to whisper a message. This message is heard by all creatures within 120 feet wearing a linked Vola'khesh. Magical silence, 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, or 3 feet of wood will block this effect, but the magic doesn't have to follow a straight line and can travel freely around corners or through openings.

entries.name: Kra'uul: Dreambound Items
entries: The chot'uul monks, who guard the dreams of Dhakaan, craft objects that are drawn to Dal Quor with a dreamer. When you dream, your Kra'uul objects accompany you. The physical object remains with your body in Eberron, but the idea of it travels with you and you can use it while exploring Dal Quor.

Any Kra'uul made of an otherwise-mundane object is a Common magic item. Kra'uul made of other magic items are the same rarity as the standard version. While the techniques of crafting Kra'uul objects are known only to the chot'uul, the DM can introduce other dreambound objects. A cursed sword might follow its bearer even into dreams, while a powerful Artifact could be even more glorious when seen in Dal Quor.

item.name: Vadalis Band
additionalEntries: {@note Duplicated from {@item Ring of Animal Influence|XDMG}}
entries: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Handling|EFA}}
This ring has 3 charges, and it regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the ring, you can expend 1 charge to cast one of the following spells (save {@dc 13}) from it:

item.name: Uul'kur (Dream Key)
entries: This iron token is inlaid with a sliver of a Siberys dragonshard. Most are worn as brooches, but others take the form of coins or keys. While an Uul'kur is a Common magic item, the secret of their creation is known only to the chot'uul monks of the Heirs of Dhakaan, and they are largely unknown in the Five Nations.

When you sleep with an Uul'kur on your person, you remain fully lucid when you dream, and when you wake, you clearly remember everything that transpired. If you understand the workings of the Uul'kur, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to bind it to your dreams until the next dawn. While bound, any creature who sleeps with this token on its person shares your dream instead of creating its own, provided you are asleep at the same time.

item.name: Tools of the Master
item.reqAttune: by a Character Proficient with the Tool
entries: While using this tool as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}, you gain a bonus to spell attack rolls. The bonus is determined by the tool's rarity. In addition, you can add this bonus to any ability check you make using this tool.

item.name: Tongueworm
entries: This coil of muscle terminates in a sharp barb. When you attune to it, this daelkyr-bred worm attaches to your throat and nestles under your tongue. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} with the worm, using your choice of Strength or Dexterity for the attack. On a hit, you deal Piercing damage equal to {@dice 1d4} + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice), instead of the normal damage of an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. In addition, the target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

item.name: Thurimbar Rod
entries: This rod is a magical {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB} developed by the gnomes of Zilargo. While holding the rod, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to produce auditory illusions that unerringly replicate the sound of any instrument with which you're proficient, with an effect similar to the {@spell Minor Illusion|XPHB} spell, with the sound emanating from the rod. To determine the quality of the performance, make a Charisma check with the {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB} you're replicating. If you are proficient with the Thurimbar Rod, you can produce unearthly music unlike any natural instrument.

item.name: Thuranni Cloak
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA}
entries: While you wear this cloak, it magically projects an illusion that makes you appear to be standing in a place near your actual location, causing any creature to have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against you. If you take damage, the property ceases to function until the start of your next turn. This property is suppressed while your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is 0.

item.name: Throwing Scarab
entries: Bred by the daelkyr Valaara, this bizarre symbiont burrows into the palm of its host, secreting razor-sharp chitin blades that can also be used as throwing weapons. When you attune to the scarab, it fuses with one of your hands, visible only as an iridescent, chitinous growth on your palm.

For every attack you make as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can extrude a shard of razor-sharp chitin from the symbiont into your empty hand, using it for the attack. The shard counts as a magical Simple Melee weapon with which you are proficient. It has the {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse}, {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light}, and {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} properties with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet. On a hit, it deals {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage and {@damage 1d4} Acid damage. The shard dissolves as soon as it hits or misses its target.

entries.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

item.name: Talking Wand
entries: While you are holding this wand, your voice and other sounds you produce are three times as loud as normal. House Phiarlan makes use of a similar device, the Thunderous Amulet, that leaves the wearer's hands free.

item.name: Storm's Embrace
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Storm|EFA}
additionalEntries: {@note Duplicated from {@item Ring of Feather Falling|XDMG}}
entries: When you fall while wearing this ring, you descend 60 feet per round and take no damage from falling.

item.name: Storm Dragonmark Reservoir
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Storm|EFA}
entries: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Storm|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Storm|EFA}
entries: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.

While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your {@feat Mark of Storm|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Storm|EFA}
entries: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

entries: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 {@action Magic|XPHB} action to instead be cast as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Duration
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.

items.name: Range

items.name: Regaining Charges
entries: The wand regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

item.name: Spellburrow
entries: These scarab-like symbionts, bred by the daelkyr Valaara, have brilliant, iridescent shells. To attune to it, you must place it on your head; during the process of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, it burrows through your skull, establishing a psychic connection with you. While it lacks human consciousness, it possesses a strange alien sentience that responds to your desires. There are tales of rare Spellburrows that possess greater knowledge and sentience; such stories sometimes end with the Spellburrow consuming the brain of the wizard who pushed it too far—but these are surely just fanciful stories!

A Spellburrow knows one cantrip of the DM's choice drawn from the Sorcerer or Warlock spell list, and you can cast this cantrip as if you know it. In addition, a Spellburrow knows one level 1 spell and one level 2 spell from the same spell list its cantrip is from. If you have the Spellcasting or Pact Magic class feature, you can cast these spells as if you had prepared them, and they don't count against the number of spells you can prepare. You can choose to use either your Intelligence modifier, or a spellcasting ability modifier you have gained from another source, for these spells.

entries.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

item.name: Spark
entries: This small oval stone is engraved with Fernian glyphs. While you are holding the stone, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to touch a candle, torch, small campfire, or similar object, instantly igniting it into flame.

item.name: Soarsled
entries: A soarsled is a crystalline disk 5 feet in diameter. It can carry a passenger through the air, using the same principles as the buttresses that sustain the towers of Sharn.

While within Sharn or another Syranian manifest zone, you can stand on the sled and take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to mentally activate it, causing it to hover beneath you. Once per turn, you can mentally command the hovering sled to move up to 30 feet in any direction. The sled can carry up to 400 pounds, and stops hovering when you step off it.
Each turn, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to make a DC 12 Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) check, moving the sled up to an additional 60 feet on a success.

While outside a Syranian manifest zone, the plane's energies rapidly fade, and the Soarsled can only be activated once, by taking a {@action Magic|XPHB} action. When it has been used to fly for a total of 10 minutes, or when you deactivate it by stepping off it, it loses its energy and can't be used again until it spends at least 8 hours in a Syranian manifest zone.

item.name: Silent Weapon

entries: This magic weapon grants a {=bonusWeapon} bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. When you are hidden from a creature and miss it with a Ranged weapon attack made with this weapon, making the attack doesn't reveal your position.

This magic weapon grants a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. When you are hidden from a creature and miss it with a Ranged weapon attack made with this weapon, making the attack doesn't reveal your position.

item.name: Shadow Sibling
entries: Crafted by Dyrrn the Corruptor, this black jewel-like object fuses to the center of your forehead when you attune to it. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can cause the sibling to exude or retract an ectoplasmic shadow that surrounds your body and conceals you from prying eyes. While the shadow is active, Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks made to see you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks made to {@action Hide|XPHB}.

In addition, when you are hit by an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend one Hit Die to shield yourself. Roll the die and add the result to your AC, including against the triggering attack. This bonus lasts until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

item.name: Shadow Dragonmark Reservoir
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA}

While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA}

While holding it, you can cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. items.name: Duration

items.name: Range
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.

items.name: Regaining Charges
entries: The wand regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

item.name: Shaarat'doovol, the Blade of Truth
entries: This blade was forged in khaar'draguus, the lava pits below Sharn, and wielded by an ancient Dhakaani hero who fell in battle against the daelkyr Belashyrra. A sentience lies within the blade; it doesn't communicate with words, but while attuned, you can feel its emotions and desires. Shaarat'doovol was forged to protect the innocent from the machinations of the daelkyr, and if it feels you are serving that purpose, it can grant great power.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit an Aberration with this weapon, the Aberration takes an extra {@damage 2d10} Radiant damage.

entries.name: Unyielding Duty
entries: If you have the favor of the sword, it guides you and shields you from unnatural influences. While wielding this sword, it can choose to grant you the following benefits:

items.name: Truesight
entries: You gain {@sense Truesight|XPHB} with a range of 90 feet.

items.name: Fortified Mind
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Psychic damage.

item.name: Serpentine Mirror
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA}
entries: The typical crystal ball, a very rare item, is about 6 inches in diameter. While touching it, you can cast the {@spell Scrying|XPHB} spell (save {@dc 17}) with it.

item.name: Sentinel Dragonmark Reservoir
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Sentinel|EFA}
entries: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Sentinel|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

item.name: Sentinel Dragonmark Channel
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Sentinel|EFA}
entries: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.

While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your {@feat Mark of Sentinel|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

item.name: Sentinel Channeling Wand
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Sentinel|EFA}
entries: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Sentinel|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

items.name: Casting Time
entries: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 {@action Magic|XPHB} action to instead be cast as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Duration
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.

items.name: Range
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.

items.name: Regaining Charges
entries: The wand regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

item.name: Rod of Wild Dominion
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Handling|EFA}
entries: This rod of varnished oak is capped at both ends with a Siberys dragonshard. While holding the rod, you can use any of its properties:

entries.name: Dominion
entries: You can cast {@spell Dominate Beast|XPHB} from the rod. When you cast the spell in this manner, the duration increases to up to 1 hour. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this spell. After the rod is used to cast this spell, it can't be used to do so again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Handling
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling|XPHB}) and Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks.

entries.name: Wild Speech
entries: You can cast {@spell Speak with Animals|XPHB} from the rod.

item.name: Resistance Breaker

entries: This magic weapon has 5 charges. When you hit a creature with it, you can expend 1 of the weapon's charges to negate all of the creature's {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} to damage until the end of your next turn. The weapon regains {@dice 1d4 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn.

This magic weapon has 5 charges. When you hit a creature with it, you can expend 1 of the weapon's charges to negate all of the creature's {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} to damage until the end of your next turn. The weapon regains {@dice 1d4 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn.

base.name: Lance
entries: A Lance requires two hands to wield when you aren't mounted.

specificVariant.name: Resistance Breaker Lance
entries: A Lance requires two hands to wield when you aren't mounted.

item.name: Quiver of Energy
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose one of the following damage types: Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison. The first time each turn that you hit a target with a weapon attack using ammunition drawn from this quiver, the attack deals an extra {@damage 1d6} damage of the chosen type.

item.name: Prospector's Wand
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Finding|EFA}
entries: This Y-shaped wand, bearing the emblem of the {@feat Mark of Finding|EFA}, has 5 charges. While holding the wand, you can use any of its properties:

entries.name: Finding
entries: You can expend 2 charges to cast {@spell Locate Creature|XPHB} from it.

entries.name: Location
entries: You can expend 1 charge to cast {@spell Locate Object|XPHB} from it.

entries.name: Prospecting
entries: You can expend 1 charge to cast {@spell Locate Animals or Plants|XPHB} from it, with the following benefits.
You can describe or name a specific kind of mineral and locate it instead of a Beast or Plant.

You can specify the minimum quantity of that Beast, Plant, or mineral that you wish the spell to find within a 30-foot-radius sphere, such as "at least 3 pounds of Eberron dragonshards" or "at least five deer." You learn the direction and distance to the closest occurrence in that {@status Concentration|XPHB}, if any are present.

entries.name: Regaining Charges
entries: The wand regains {@dice 1d4 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

item.name: Ori Boots
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Passage|EFA}
entries: While you wear these boots, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to click the boots' heels together. If you do, the boots double your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and any creature that makes an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} against you has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack roll. If you click your heels together again, you end the effect.
When you've used the boots' property for a total of 10 minutes, the magic ceases to function for you until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

item.name: Medi Spectacles
additionalEntries: {@note Duplicated from {@item Eyes of Minute Seeing|XDMG}}
entries: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Detection|EFA}}

These crystal lenses fit over the eyes. While wearing them, your vision improves significantly out to a range of 1 foot, granting you {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} within that range and {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks made to examine something within that range.

item.name: Medani Dowser
entries: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Detection|EFA}}

This wand has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. While holding it, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to expend 1 charge, and if a secret door or trap is within 60 feet of you, the wand pulses and points at the one nearest to you.

item.name: Manor Key
entries: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Hospitality|EFA}}

This long key, studded with tiny Siberys dragonshards, can only be used by a creature with the {@feat Mark of Hospitality|EFA}. You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to trace the outline of a door in the air with the key and cast {@spell Mordenkainen's Magnificent Mansion|XPHB} without requiring Material components. The spell ends after 24 hours or when you use the key to lock the door and dismiss the effect; at that time, any creatures within the mansion are expelled into an open space near its entrance. Once used, the key cannot be used again until the next dawn.

item.name: Lamplighter
entries: While you are holding this wand, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to instantaneously light or snuff out a candle, torch, small campfire, or similar source of flame within 10 feet of you.

item.name: Kundar Chains
entries: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA}}

You can take a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to place these shackles on a creature that has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. The shackles adjust to fit a creature of Small to Large size. The shackles prevent a creature bound by them from using any method of extradimensional movement, including teleportation or travel to a different plane of existence. They don't prevent the creature from passing through an interdimensional portal.

You and any creature you designate when you use the shackles can take a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to remove them. Once every 30 days, the bound creature can make a {@dc 30} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check. On a successful check, the creature breaks free and destroys the shackles.

item.name: Keeper's Fang
entries: These infamous weapons, prized by assassins, have a Khyber dragonshard embedded into the pommel that channels the souls of victims, but doesn't itself trap them. There's much debate over the actual fate of the souls of those slain by a Keeper's Fang. Common myth says that the souls of victims are trapped in the Lair of the Keeper, and heroes can seek to reclaim a soul from the Sovereign of Death and Decay. Another myth maintains that these weapons channel souls to the overlord Katashka, and that one must deal with the Lords of Dust to restore a victim. Most Keeper's Fangs were created by the Shaarat'khesh assassins of the Empire of Dhakaan. Rather than ascribing the blade's power to the Keeper--whose existence the Dhakaani reject--they believe these blades utterly destroy the souls of their victims.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Whenever you use it to reduce a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the creature is slain and its soul removed. A creature whose soul has been stolen in this way can be restored to life only by means of a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell.

item.name: Jora Charm
item.reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Healing|EFA}
additionalEntries: {@note Duplicated from {@item Periapt of Wound Closure|XDMG}}
entries: While wearing this pendant, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Life Preservation
entries: Whenever you make a {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB}, you can change a roll of 9 or lower to a 10, turning a failed save into a successful one.

entries.name: Natural Healing Boost
entries: Whenever you roll a {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die} to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, double the number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} it restores.

item.name: Integrated Tool
entries: {@note Requires Use by a {@race Warforged|EFA}}

This item attaches to the body of a warforged, and is designed to serve as one of the following tools that weighs 10 pounds or less: an {@item Artisan's Tool|XPHB|Artisan's Tools}, {@item Forgery Kit|XPHB}, {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB}, {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB}, {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, or a {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB}.

You must incorporate the tool into your body before you can use it. Over the course of 1 hour, you can attach the tool or remove it from your body, remaining in contact with it for the whole hour; this can be done over a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

While you're alive, the tool can't be removed from your body against your will. Though the tool has become part of your body, you must still have a hand free to make use of it. You can only have one Integrated Tool attached to your body at a time.

entries.name: Warforged and Prosthetic Limbs
entries: {@book Eberron: Rising from the Last War|ERLW} introduces the {@item Prosthetic Limb|XDMG}, a Common magic item requiring {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} which predates the warforged. Prosthetic Limbs come in many forms; one might resemble an organic limb of animated wood, and another could be a metal shell or a construct of force. During the Last War, Karrnath made use of skeletal prosthetics, and more recently, Cannith and Jorasco have produced prosthetics that use the same semiorganic materials as the warforged.

Eberron: Rising from the Last War also includes two magic items designed to integrate into a Warforged's forearm: the {@item Armblade|ERLW} and the {@item Wand Sheath|ERLW}. At the DM's discretion, a character of a different species might be able to integrate one of these warforged items into their Prosthetic Limb; the question is if the two can logically work together, or if the style of your prosthetic makes it implausible that it could mesh with a warforged component. If the DM decides it's possible to integrate a component item with the prosthetic, the two could be counted as a single magic item for the purpose of determining the number of magic items you can attune to. If you remove the component from the prosthetic, you immediately lose your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to the component.

item.name: Hungry Weapon

entries: A creation of the daelkyr, this weapon is formed from muscle and bone. It may moan, growl, or wail, and it twists in your grip if it doesn't like you. If any creature attempts to wield this weapon while not attuned to it, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls made using the weapon. Additionally, if you are attuned to this weapon when another creature tries to wield it, the weapon's hilt extrudes sharp thorns and that creature takes {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage each turn.

While attuned to and wielding this weapon, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to bond to it, causing tendrils from the hilt of the weapon to burrow into your flesh. You can end the weapon's bond as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, causing the tendrils to retract so you can release the weapon. You can remain attuned to the weapon regardless of whether you're bonded to it. While bonded to it, you gain the following benefits:

items.name: Secure Grip
entries: The weapon is bound to your hand and can't be removed from your grasp, voluntarily or involuntarily. If it's a {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} weapon, only one of your hands is bound to the weapon.

items.name: Drain Life
entries: When you hit a creature with this weapon, you can choose to expend one {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Die} to deal additional damage with the attack, and as you do, drain the life from your foes. Roll the {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Die} and add your Constitution modifier; the attack deals extra Necrotic damage equal to the result, and you regain an equal number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

item.name: Houseward (Uncommon)
entries: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA}}

This engraved block of lead, approximately 1 cubic foot in size, holds an embedded Siberys dragonshard. The Houseward provides state-of-the-art magical security, and is typically embedded into the floor of the building it is supposed to protect. If any creature with the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA} spends 10 minutes touching the Houseward, it can cast {@spell Guards and Wards|XPHB} without requiring Material components. A 2,500 square foot area is protected by the spell. The duration of the spell is 24 days, but the effect ends early if the Houseward is used again to cast the spell, if a creature with the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA} spends 10 minutes touching the Houseward to end its effects, or if a Houseward is removed from the area it is currently protecting. After being used to cast the spell, the Houseward can't do so again until the next dawn.
